title: Scaled Dot-Product Attention
hook: How does a model decide which words to focus on? Scaled dot-product attention computes similarity scores, turns them into weights, and mixes values. Edit Q, K, V and see the effect.

explorations.title: Equal scores
explorations.predict: If all keys are identical, what will the attention weights be?
explorations.observe: Weights are uniform (0.5 each). Output is the average of V rows.
explorations.why: When scores are equal, softmax gives equal weights, so output is the mean of V.

explorations.title: Dominant score
explorations.predict: If one key is much more similar to the query, what happens to the weights?
explorations.observe: Weight for the first key is near 1, second near 0. Output is close to V1.
explorations.why: Large score gap makes softmax concentrate on the max score.

self_tests.name: Output equals weighted sum of V

limitation: This demo uses tiny matrices (2x2) and does not include multiple heads, masking, or training. It only illustrates the forward pass of scaled dot-product attention.
misconception: Attention weights are not learned parameters; they are computed from Q and K. The scaling factor prevents large dot products from making softmax too sharp.

claims.text: The scaling factor 1/√d_k is used to prevent the dot products from growing large.
In this toy setup, we use 2x2 matrices and omit multi-head and masking for simplicity.

outcomes.outcome: Compute similarity scores between queries and keys.
Apply softmax to obtain attention weights that sum to 1.
Compute the output as a weighted sum of values.
Explain the effect of scaling by 1/√d_k.
